chapter_title_en: Wedding of Tariel and Nestan-Darejan (in India)
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Tariel and Nestan-Darejan are crowned King and Queen of all seven kingdoms of India, rewarding the faithful Asmat with one-seventh of India as her own principality and establishing a golden age of justice, mercy, and mutual aid with Avtandil in Arabia and Pridon in Mulghazanzar ('Even the goat and the wolf fed together').

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
დედოფალმან მათ ცოლ-ქმართა თვითო ხელი დაუჭირა,
ზედა ტახტსა მეფისასა ერთგან დასხმა გაუპირა,
მოიშორვა კაეშანი, გული მდედრი აქვიტკირა,
და გლოვა ცვალა სიხარულად, აღარავინ აატირა.
stanzas.english_translation: As presents for Rostevan, he (Tariel) made him (Avt’handil) take with him beautiful little mantles, also a vessel (full) of cut gems, not spoons(ful), not ladles(ful). "Take them from me, go," quoth he, "disobey me not!" Avt’handil said: "I know not how I shall survive without thee!"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 64 ('Wedding of Tariel and Nestan-Darejan (in India)', Stanza 1634; Wardrop Stanza 1565): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Nestan-Darejan are crowned King and Queen of all seven kingdoms of India, rewarding the faithful Asmat with one-seventh of India as her own principality and establishing a golden age of justice, mercy, and mutual aid with Avtandil in Arabia and Pridon in Mulghazanzar ('Even the goat and the wolf fed together').

stanzas.english_translation: The lady (Nestan) sent to the lady (T’hinat’hin) a little cloak and a veil; who save hers was worthy of such garments! A jewel--he who carried it off could not say: "I have carried it in vain!"--at night it gives light like the sun; it is visible wherever thou lookest.

stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil mounted, he departed, he said farewell to Taria, the flame of the fire of separation burned them both; all the Indians wept, the tear moistened the mead. Avt’handil said: "The poison of this world slays me!"

stanzas.english_translation: P’hridon and Avt’handil journeyed together for a few days; the road separated them, each went his way weeping; the things they had planned had turned out well for them; Avt’handil came to Arabia, he had not seen troubles in vain.

stanzas.english_translation: The Arabs came forth to meet him, he beautified the realm; he saw his sun, the affliction of his desires fled; he sat with her on the throne, he rejoiced at the joy of the onlookers. The Most High from above endued his crown with sovereignty.

stanzas.english_translation: Those three sovereigns loved one another, they visited one another, their desires were fulfilled, they that disputed their rule were put to the sword, they enlarged their kingdoms, they were sovereign, they increased their might.
